title: VPC token-shedder probe gate and saturation-aware SLO orchestration
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background:
Redwood Private deployments need robust health probes that do more than binary up/down checks. During peak token load and upgrade windows we see amplification effects across the token pipeline (enqueue growth, KV cache pressure, and backend tail latency). Existing probes surface symptoms but don't coordinate shedding or graceful degradation.

Goal:
Implement a probe orchestration layer (Probe Gate) for VPC private workers that: 1) emits unified SLO metrics (latency quantiles, error-rate, token throughput, queue depth, and GPU saturation), 2) exposes a token-shedding signal when safe thresholds are breached, and 3) integrates with Terraform/IaC and rollout automation so probes and remediation policies are versioned and can be toggled per-environment.

Proposal highlights:
- New probe agent (lightweight sidecar) that calculates per-worker rolling windows for: request p50/p95/p99, model error-rate, token throughput (tokens/s), queue depth, and GPU/CPU utilization.
- Token-shedder policy: when token throughput drops below a configured watermark and queue depth > threshold or GPU util > 85%, emit a shedding hint to the router with graded severity (informational -> delay -> reject) instead of immediate hard failure.
- Orchestration: a controller that aggregates worker-level signals into cluster-level SLOs and pushes remediation actions (scale up/down, fallback to compatible model variant, or enable degraded response mode).
- IaC: Publish Terraform modules and a Helm chart for sidecar + controller. Modules expose tunables (window_seconds, p99_threshold_ms, error_rate_pct, gpu_util_pct, shedding_policy).
- Observability: Export metrics to metrics-backend with standardized labels (env, region, customer_tier, model_name). Create dashboards and alerting rules for SLO burn rate and shedding events.
- Rollout & Safety: Canary rollout by region + automatic rollback if canary SLOs regress. Provide a runbook for manual intervention and a dry-run mode in the controller to validate rules against historical telemetry.

Key design trade-offs:
- Local vs central aggregation: local sidecar gives faster detection but noisier signals; central aggregation reduces noise but increases detection latency. We use hybrid: local fast path for shedding hints, central for final policy decisions.
- Shedding granularity: per-request rejection harms UX; prefer graded delay/queue-priority and preferring low-cost fallbacks where possible.
- Tight thresholds reduce risk of overload but increase false positives; provide conservative defaults and per-customer tuning.

Acceptance criteria (must be all true for Done):
- A Terraform module and Helm chart published in infra-modules with docs and example (private-dev, private-prod) (link required). 
- Sidecar + controller deployed to a private staging environment and exercised with a load generator that simulates token spikes and model faults. 
- Metrics emitted: vpc.worker.request_pxx_ms (p50/p95/p99), vpc.worker.error_rate_pct, vpc.worker.tokens_per_sec, vpc.worker.queue_depth, vpc.worker.gpu_util_pct. Metrics conform to label conventions. 
- Token-shedder outputs observed in routing logs and an automated rollback triggered in a canary test when configured thresholds exceeded. 
- Dashboard and alert runbooks created; SLO burn-rate alerts fire during simulated regression. 
- Security review completed and KMS/credentials usage documented for controller-to-router communication. 

Deliverables and links (placeholders - to update with PRs/Confluence):
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-42879+Token-Shedder-Probe-Gate (draft)
- Terraform module repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules/tree/main/vpc-probe-gate (WIP)
- Helm chart: https://github.com/redwood-inference/k8s-charts/pulls/412 (draft)
- Load test harness: https://perf.redwood.ai/scenarios/probe-shedder-spike

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy sidecar and controller to internal staging (private-staging) in dry-run mode. Run synthetic spike tests for 72h.
2) Gradual canary to a single customer region with monitoring on SLOs for 48h.
3) If canary stable, increase to 25% traffic; monitor for 7d.
4) Full rollout with adjustable thresholds.

Longer-term ideas (not in scope this ticket):
- ML-based anomaly detector for adaptive shedding thresholds.
- Integration with Experimentation platform for A/B testing degraded modes.
